record.name: Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program
record.administeredBy: U.S. Department of Agriculture, administered by the Wisconsin Department of Health Services (WIC); local agencies are county Aging and Disability Resource Centers
record.summary: Vouchers for older adults with limited income to buy fresh, locally grown produce at Wisconsin farmers markets and farmstands.
record.benefit: Five $5.00 checks ($25.00 total) per person per growing season (June 1 through October 31) for fresh fruits, vegetables, and herbs grown in or near Wisconsin.

steps: Contact your local agency -- usually your county's Aging and Disability Resource Center (ADRC).
Complete the SFMNP Eligibility Agreement (form F-40103), self-certifying age, residency, and income.
Receive your checks and a list of participating markets and farmstands.

record.seasonalNote: Checks are valid June 1 through October 31. Enrollment opens seasonally through local agencies; supplies are limited.

scopeColocated.scopeLocation: NOT on the program's public web page at all -- the page says only 'Meet income guidelines'. The percentage is on the self-certification FORM (F-40103), and the actual dollar thresholds are on yet a third document, the annual 'SFMNP Income Eligibility Table'. Three documents deep to get from 'there is an income test' to 'here is the number'.

cost.notes: 2 fetches + 1 search. The public page was a dead end for the figure; the application form PDF had the 185% self-certification language. Did not fetch the separate Income Eligibility Table (would give the current dollar rows).

surprises: A one-sentence eligibility rule ('60+, WI resident, meet income guidelines') where the single load-bearing number is deliberately kept off the public page and split across two downstream forms. If an extractor only reads the page it was handed, it authors a record with an income test it cannot fill.
